findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definitions silently override each other
findings.body: The file now defines `OptimizedImage.downsize` twice: once at line 145 with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and again at line 149 with `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not support overloading; the second definition silently replaces the first. Any existing caller that passes width and height as separate arguments (the original 4-argument API, e.g. `downsize(from, to, 800, 600)`) will now raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (4 for 2..3)`. The overload must be removed or the signatures unified (e.g. accept *args and dispatch).

findings.title: Downsize loop never breaks on failure and uploads oversized file anyway
findings.body: In `create_upload`, the `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...` loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` but ignores its return value. If `convert` fails (returns false) or the image simply cannot be shrunk below the limit within 5 iterations, the code falls through and calls `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized (or unchanged) tempfile anyway, retrying an identical failing operation up to 5 times and wasting CPU. If downsizing fails or the file is still over the limit after the attempts, the upload should be rejected with a clear error instead of proceeding.

findings.title: Animated GIFs are destroyed or fail downsizing
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` routes animated GIFs (when `allow_animation` is true) to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` producing `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%` — gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects geometry like `WxH`, not a percentage, so the command fails and the GIF is never reduced (and the loop retries the same failing command 5 times). When `allow_animation` is false, `downsize_instructions` uses `#{from}[0]`, which silently strips all but the first frame, turning users' animated GIFs into static images. Additionally the animated-vs-static decision keys off `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but the tempfile path (e.g. `discourse-upload-image...`) has no `.gif` extension, so animated handling never actually triggers. Note also that the `from` and `to` paths are identical, so `convert` reads and overwrites the same file each iteration with compounding quality loss.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit ignores per-type site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously enforced `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (different limits for images vs attachments); it now hardcodes 10MB for both. If an admin configures `max_attachment_size_kb` above or below 10MB, or `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB, the client-side validation no longer matches the server: users may be wrongly blocked from uploading valid files, or allowed to select files the server will reject — and the 413 error handler at line 246 also reports the hardcoded 10MB rather than the actual configured limit, producing misleading error messages.

findings.title: API URL downloads now hardcode 10MB instead of the configured image size
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Sites that set `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB (e.g. 15MB) will now have API-based URL image downloads truncated/rejected at 10MB even though the subsequent downsize step could have brought them under the limit, and sites with a limit below 10MB now download more data than configured. The download cap should stay tied to the setting (or a named constant larger than any supported limit).
